sentences.text: Padillasaurus was a medium-sized titanosauriform sauropod that lived during the Early Cretaceous Barremian stage in Colombia.
Based on limited remains, the animal may have reached 16 to 18 meters in length and weighed about 10 tonnes.
The dinosaur is distinguished by its tail vertebrae being weakly expanded to the sides with divided side projections.
The vertebrae of Padillasaurus are opisthocoelic, featuring a convex front and concave back.
These bones possess large pleurocoels, which are pneumatic processes connecting to hollow cavities within the bone.
An additional lamina was present on the spine between the diapophysis and the vertebral body.
The neural arches are positioned relatively forward and feature long ridges running between joint face protuberances and the vertebral body.
The side projections on the vertebrae are oriented obliquely backward and have a convex lower area.
The tail vertebrae have a height equal to half their width.
Padillasaurus represents the first record of a Cretaceous brachiosaurid from South America, whereas previous Cretaceous brachiosaurid findings were only known from North America.
It is the latest known brachiosaurid from the ancient continent of Gondwana.
Local farmers discovered the fossil of Padillasaurus in a limestone nodule in Ricaurte, Colombia, during the 1990s.
Padillasaurus was first described and named in 2015 by José L. Carballido and colleagues.
The genus name Padillasaurus honors Carlos Bernardo Padilla, founder of the Centro de Investigaciones Paleontológicas in Villa de Leyva.
The species name leivaensis refers to Villa de Leyva, near the discovery site of the holotype.
The known fossils of Padillasaurus consist of torso, sacral, and tail vertebrae presumed to belong to a single individual.
The holotype specimen JACVM 0001 includes a rear dorsal vertebra, the last two sacral vertebrae, and the first eight caudal vertebrae without chevrons.
Ammonite fossils in the rock matrix date the formation to the late Barremian, approximately 130 million years ago.
It lacks a typical Cretaceous North American brachiosaurid trait: the anterior caudal vertebral spinous process angles backward instead of slightly forward.
Padillasaurus was initially classified as a brachiosaurid and considered the first named South American brachiosaurid.
A more recent study reclassified Padillasaurus as a basal member of the Somphospondyli.
Padillasaurus was initially placed in the family Brachiosauridae based on its morphology.
Cavities in the sacral vertebrae lacking connection to the hollow interior, a lack of true pleurocoel, linked Padillasaurus to brachiosaurids.
Cladistic analysis found Padillasaurus in a polytomy with other basal forms like Abydosaurus, Brachiosaurus, and Giraffatitan, with Cedarosaurus and Venenosaurus occasionally as sister taxa.
Padillasaurus is classified within the unranked family Somphospondyli.
Padillasaurus was originally classified in the family Brachiosauridae based on its morphology.
The dinosaur has cavities in the sacral vertebrae that do not connect to the hollow interior of the vertebra, meaning it lacks a true pleurocoel.
This trait relates it to the brachiosaurids.

A cladistic analysis could not determine exact relationships, placing Padillasaurus in a basal polytomy with Abydosaurus, Brachiosaurus, Giraffatitan, Cedarosaurus, and Venenosaurus, which sometimes became sister taxa.
Its parent group is Somphospondyli.
It belongs to the class Saurischia.
It lived during the Barremian stage, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
